subject: Marketplace vs PO — procurement preference & timeline (post-call)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie LeGrand <sophie.legrand@finserv.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace vs PO — procurement preference & timeline (post-call)

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap from discovery:
- Primary goal: speed up rollout of LLM-powered recommendations for loan underwriting pipelines (pilot: ~3k requests/day).
- Security: data stays in your VPC for private deployment but billing still needs procurement clarity.
- Budget: leadership approved $75k for Q3 POC but procurement controls payment method.

Open questions / asks:
1) Procurement preference — AWS Marketplace (consolidated billing, faster onboarding) vs. traditional PO to Redwood (Net30). Which path is procurement leaning toward?
2) If PO is required, can you share the procurement contact + PO template or instructions?
3) What is your internal approval timeline? (target kickoff window from your team)

Why this matters: Marketplace onboarding typically gets customers running in 3–5 business days once the team signs up, while PO + legal redlines tend to add 1–3 weeks depending on review cycles. If you prefer the marketplace, we can draft a short MAP and loop in our marketplace enablement rep to speed it.

Attaching: redwood-pricing-quote-v2.pdf (PDF) — includes marketplace & PO pricing rows for comparison.

Proposed next step: 30-min call with procurement + engineering to finalize path. My availability: Tue 5/12 10:00–12:00 PT or Wed 5/13 14:00–16:00 PT.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-pricing-quote-v2.pdf (PDF, 1 page)
From: Sophie LeGrand <sophie.legrand@finserv.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finserv.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace vs PO — procurement preference & timeline (post-call)

Jordan — thanks for the clear note and the quote. Quick answers: 

- Preference: Our procurement team prefers AWS Marketplace for SaaS where possible, but our policy requires a PO for any vendor spend > $50k unless the vendor can be processed through Marketplace with an approved contract.
- Timeline: Procurement meets weekly on Tuesdays; earliest they would approve a PO is the 2-week cycle (so likely by end of next week if we start now).
- Contacts: looping in procurement@finserv.com — they own PO issuance and vendor onboarding.

I've attached our standard procurement questionnaire — it has the fields they'll need. Also can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a PO (Net30) if Marketplace onboarding isn't feasible?

Best,
Sophie LeGrand
Head of Platform
FinServ Technologies

--
Attachment: finserv-procurement-questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie LeGrand <sophie.legrand@finserv.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace vs PO — procurement preference & timeline (post-call)

Thanks Sophie — really helpful. Short answers here and a proposed MAP: 

1) PO vs Marketplace: Redwood supports both: we can accept a PO (Net30) and will work through any required billing details. That said, AWS Marketplace tends to be faster for onboarding, provides consolidated AWS billing for you, and removes the need for a standalone invoice flow from our side. Marketplace also allows you to use existing AWS purchasing controls if your finance team prefers that.

2) If procurement requires PO: we will engage legal to review standard terms (we've seen redlines on indemnity and data clauses — usually 3–5 business days for standard redlines). Finance at Redwood can accept PO on Net30.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) / timeline (draft):
- Day 0 (today): share procurement questionnaire (thanks) + price comparison (attached).
- Day 1–5: Redwood and FinServ legal review marketplace T&Cs or PO terms; Redwood to share a short MAP draft.
- Week 2: Procurement issues PO OR completes Marketplace enablement; once signed, provisioning + kickoff within 3 business days.

Attaching: mutual_action_plan-draft.docx (Draft MAP — editable). Please let me know if you want a variant that explicitly calls out SOC 2 evidence or on-prem deployment clauses.

Can we set a 30-min sync with procurement this Tue 5/12 at 10:30 PT? If procurement is unavailable at that time, propose alternate Tues slot.

Thanks — looping Rafael and Marissa to coordinate marketplace enablement and billing.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--

- Marketplace rep: I'll reach out to our AWS Marketplace rep (aws-mktplace@amazon.com) to get the enablement checklist and expected timing.
- If you end up on PO: our finance ops can process Net30 PO terms; we'll need a signed PO document and vendor form.

Jordan — Marissa will handle the technical onboarding once we confirm the procurement route. Marissa, can you prep an enablement checklist and estimate hours for the pilot (engineering + infra)?
